question: (i) What is the direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave if $\vec{E}$ is along $+\hat{i}$ and $\vec{B}$ is along $+\hat{j}$? (ii) What will happen to the direction of propagation if $\vec{B}$ is reversed?

options.A:
(i) $+\hat{i}\times+\hat{j}=-\hat{k}$, so the wave propagates along $-\hat{k}$.
(ii) Reversing $\vec{B}$ leaves the propagation direction unchanged.
options.B:
(i) The wave propagates along $+\hat{i}$ because the electric field determines the direction.
(ii) Reversing $\vec{B}$ makes it propagate along $-\hat{i}$.
options.C:
(i) Propagation is along $\vec{E}\times\vec{B}$; thus $+\hat{i}\times+\hat{j}=+\hat{k}$.
(ii) If $\vec{B}$ reverses to $-\hat{j}$, then $+\hat{i}\times(-\hat{j})=-\hat{k}$, so propagation reverses.
options.D:
(i) The wave propagates along $+\hat{j}$.
(ii) Reversing $\vec{B}$ makes the propagation direction $+\hat{k}$.
